minutes.headline: Select Board continued the Main Street liquor license transfer, approved Bedrock Bar and Grill, and backed Flat Hill Road advisory signs.
minutes.summary: The board ratified two appointments, continued one liquor license transfer hearing to October 15 over missing application items, and approved another transfer. It accepted the DPW and police Flat Hill Road traffic report, heard the interim town manager's report, discussed an APDC warrant article on selling the Brooks House, and reviewed an ARPA contingency plan. It also adopted FY25 goals and approved some minutes.

public_comment.topic: Unanswered public records requests, a zoning board of appeals matter over a shed on HOA common land, and complaints about HOA attorneys and remarks by town officials.

votes.motion: Ratify interim town manager's appointment of Evelyn Row as Public Safety front desk clerk.
Continue the St Mary in Christ license transfer public hearing to October 15 at 7:15 p.m.
Approve transfer of alcohol and related licenses to Bedrock Bar and Grill LLC, 324 Electric Avenue Unit 4.
Accept DPW director and police chief report on Flat Hill Road and adopt the advisory signs at nine locations.
Ratify appointment of seasonal cemetery laborers Nicholas Green and Autumn Buck.
Adopt Select Board goals for fiscal year 25.
Approve minutes of November 14, 2023 as written.

budget_items.what_was_said: A new 24-month contract with First Point Power raises the supply rate for enrolled residents, still lower than the utility's basic service rate.

The interim town manager said the building's budget deficit was eliminated by finding money elsewhere in the facilities budget, and said the school department has paid its rent. He said a specific operating budget for the building will be requested.

budget_items.topic: Fall town meeting funding / free cash
budget_items.what_was_said: No free cash will be used at the fall town meeting; overlay surplus will be used instead. FY24 close-out is near.
The interim town manager described small unreconciled differences in two departments that may hit free cash later.
Interim town manager proposed buying DPW trucks with ARPA instead of capital money, applying ARPA underruns to overruns, and possibly funding a food pantry allocation.
Members recalled the original ARPA allocation for an ambulance and dump trucks, with the total just under a million.
An accounts payable warrant was presented for signature.

decisions.decision: Interim town manager suggested conferring with owner, buyers and counsel before the continued St Mary in Christ hearing, set for October 15.
Report on Flat Hill Road to be posted on the web, with a letter and link mailed to area residents in about two weeks, coming from the board.
Interim town manager to meet with the APDC within a week to reword the Brooks House article, possibly as a select board article; APDC to try for a quorum.
The school committee, specifically Mr Beardmore, to be engaged about the Brooks House parcel.
Draft fall town meeting warrant to be sent next Tuesday with final vote on October 15; short executive session on interim police chief contract set for about 6:45 next Tuesday.
No meeting the week of Thanksgiving.

what_happened.line: The Select Board continued the St Mary in Christ liquor license transfer hearing to October 15 at 7:15 p.m., with the vote unanimous.
The board approved the transfer of alcohol and related licenses to Bedrock Bar and Grill LLC on Electric Avenue, unanimously.
The board accepted the DPW and police report on Flat Hill Road and adopted advisory signs at nine locations, unanimously.
The interim town manager said no free cash will be used at fall town meeting and overlay surplus will be used instead.
The interim town manager was directed to meet the APDC within a week to reword the Brooks House warrant article, and the board adopted its FY25 goals.

why_it_matters: The fall town meeting warrant will not draw on free cash, and the Brooks House parcel article is being reworded, so residents may be asked to vote on a property sale article.
Flat Hill Road drivers and neighbors will see new advisory signs, and the report is to be mailed to area residents.
